What Isotop helps you do


  1. Generate a complete token system from a brand colour and a short brief
  2. Apply it to Figma as real variables, with semantic roles aliased to primitives
  3. Define and manage core color variables as a single source of truth
  4. Link and unlink design tokens to core variables, individually or in bulk
  5. Generate and evolve color palettes using reproducible recipes
  6. Work safely at scale with sandbox previews, Undo and Redo, and explicit syncing


Isotop is a professional tool for building and maintaining color and token systems in Figma, made for designers and teams working on real design systems rather than one-off color edits.


It does two jobs. It generates a token system for you, and it gives you the controls to keep the variables you already have structured and predictable, whether that is a small product or a large multi-collection system with deep dependencies.


___________________________________


Collider AI: generate the system


Collider is Isotop's AI system for token generation. Give it a brand colour and a short brief, and it builds the system in two layers: the primitives first, then the semantic roles that alias them.


Generation is guided. Collider works through the layer group by group and stops after each one, so you review colours before typography, and typography before spacing. Accept a group, edit it, regenerate it, or skip it. An accepted group can still be edited or regenerated later without disturbing the rest.


Every text-on-background pair the system implies is measured against its contrast floor while the layer is being built. When a pair falls short, the role is re-aimed at a primitive that clears it, never at a colour invented on the spot. Every role carries its value in each mode, so light and dark are one system, not two.


Nothing reaches your Figma file until you apply. Then the primitives land as variables, the semantic roles land as aliases pointing at them, type and shadow roles are compiled into named text and effect styles, and a documentation page is drawn from real Figma frames bound to the variables that were written. Each token carries its contract in the variable description, and the whole system exports to JSON.


Collider requires an Isotop account and runs on credits. Your prompt and design-system context are sent to our AI provider to generate suggestions; your account identifier and email are not.


___________________________________


Core Variables and Smart Linking


Define which variables act as core colors, the foundation and single source of truth for your system.


Once core variables are defined, design tokens can be linked to them individually or in bulk. Smart suggestions surface only the most relevant core variables, which reduces errors and removes unnecessary searching. Autolink and conflict resolution make relationships explicit and predictable, even in inherited or highly complex systems.


___________________________________


Palette Generator


The built-in Palette Generator creates balanced color palettes from a single seed color. It works with any palette structure and supports both single-mode and multi-mode systems.


Palettes are generated from reusable recipes rather than fixed presets, which makes them easy to review, refine, and safely evolve over time. All changes are previewed in a sandbox before they are applied, so nothing updates system-wide by accident.


___________________________________


Safe Sync and System Stability


Isotop is built around a non-destructive workflow. By default every change stays temporary until you explicitly sync it with Figma. Pending updates are clearly highlighted, and Undo and Redo cover all core actions, including bulk operations.


Isotop writes only into the collections it owns. A collection you created keeps its name and its contents, even when the name resembles one of ours. This is what makes it safe to experiment, refactor, and scale without breaking what already works.


___________________________________


Isotop exports collections and variables to JSON with all alias relationships preserved. A session-based Activity Log shows linking actions, detected conflicts, and system warnings, so teams can see the state of their color architecture at a glance.


Isotop reflects how modern design systems are actually built: structured, intentional, and made to scale.

model.name: Design Token Audit and Fix
model.description:
Design Token Audit & Fix scans your Figma file/page/frame for raw values that should be using design tokens and lets you fix them without leaving the plugin panel.


What it detects

  1. Colors - fill and stroke colors not bound to a color variable or style
  2. Spacing - auto-layout gap, padding values not using spacing variables
  3. Typography - text layers not linked to a text style
  4. Corner radii - raw radius values not using a radius variable
  5. Effects - drop shadows and inner shadows not linked to an effect style It checks against your local variables, local styles, and any linked library variables - so it works with both modern Variable-based design systems and older Style-based ones.


How it works

  1. Click Scan — the plugin traverses every node on the page (or just your selection) and collects all raw values
  2. A rule-based engine instantly matches each value to the closest token in your design system and assigns a confidence level (High / Medium / Low)
  3. For values with no confident match, you can optionally run AI analysis (requires a Claude API key) - Claude reads the node name and frame context to suggest the right semantic token even when multiple tokens share the same value
  4. Browse issues by category - Colors, Spacing, Typography, Radii, Effects — and filter by confidence level
  5. Click Fix to apply a token in one click, or Choose to pick from the full token list manually


Key features

  1. One-click fixes - applies variable bindings or style links directly to the node
  2. Bulk fix - apply all high-confidence suggestions at once
  3. Ignore - dismiss issues you want to leave as-is; ignored state persists across sessions
  4. Multiple libraries - works with files that link to multiple external component or token libraries
  5. Ambiguous match detection - when several tokens share the same value, the plugin flags the issue and prompts you to choose the right semantic token rather than guessing
  6. Scan scope - scan the full page or just your current selection
  7. Hidden layers - optionally include hidden layers in the audit
  8. Generate report - creates a structured audit report frame directly in your Figma file
  9. Light and dark UI - matches your OS theme or toggle manually in settings


AI analysis (optional)

The rule-based engine handles most cases without any API calls. AI analysis is an optional enhancement for values that have no confident rule-based match. It uses the Claude API (Anthropic) — you provide your own API key in Settings. You only pay for what you use, and the estimated cost is shown before you run it.


Privacy

Your design data is only sent to the Claude API when you explicitly click Analyze — and only the unmatched nodes are sent, not your entire file. No data is stored or shared by the plugin itself.

Varlint finds the values in your file that should be variables and are not, tells you which variable each one should be, and binds them.


YOUR IT REVIEW CAN CHECK THIS, NOT TAKE MY WORD

Varlint declares no network access, and Figma prints that on this page beside the last-updated date — so the person who approves plugins where you work can confirm it without contacting me. ALL 46 PLACES

Figma allows a variable in forty-six different places: sizes, spacing, corners, stroke weights, fill and stroke colour, every text property, effects, layout grids and component properties. Varlint looks at all of them. That number is not typed in by hand — a test reads Figma's own type definitions and fails if the two ever disagree.


IT SAYS WHICH VARIABLE

Finding a raw value is the easy half. If a variable in your file already holds that value, Varlint names it. If none does, it says so. It never offers to invent variables for you — your token set is yours.


DECISIONS, NOT ROWS

Varlint reads how far your file has already got in each group — colour, spacing, corners, text — and only ticks the ones you are visibly already doing. WHEN IT CAN'T, IT SAYS SO

Every binding is read back after it is written, and anything that did not take is listed with the reason: the layer is gone, the variable is gone, Figma will not allow it there. A binder that fails quietly is worse than one that fails.

Example: Figma collection color, variable background/success → color.background.success


Option B — Compare with GitHub

Click Settings in the plugin header.

Under GitHub, enter:

Owner (e.g. my-org)

Repository (e.g. design-tokens)

File path (e.g. tokens/core.json)

Default branch (e.g. main)

GitHub Personal Access Token (repo read scope)

Save Settings.

Set Source B to GitHub, choose a branch, then Fetch & Compare.

In the Inspector, select a token to see commit author, date, and message.

Option C — Compare with another Figma file

Click Settings → Figma Remote File.

Paste the file key or full URL, e.g.

https://www.figma.com/design/AbCdEf123/My-Design-System

Add a Figma Personal Access Token with file_variables:read scope.

Save Settings.

Set Source B to Figma File, then Fetch & Compare.

Requirements: Enterprise org, view access to the remote file, token scope file_variables:read.

Source B is read-only; apply always updates the current file.


3. Review the diff

Left panel — categories with change counts [+added][~modified][-removed]

Center panel — diff rows with checkboxes, color swatches, old/new values

Right panel (Inspector) — click a token for warnings, alias chain, impact, WCAG contrast, preview

Rows with ⚠ show alias-break or naming warnings.


4. Stage and apply changes

Use checkboxes to select tokens to apply (added/modified only; removed tokens are not auto-deleted).

Footer shows: Selected: X tokens to update, Y to ignore.

Reject All — clears all selections.

Apply Selected Changes — writes selected values into the current file’s Variables.

Use Cmd/Ctrl + Z in Figma if you need to undo.

5. Configure quality rules (optional)

Open Settings:


SettingPurpose

Naming convention

Lint new tokens (kebab-case, camelCase, snake_case)

Pattern (regex)

Stricter path validation

Max depth

Limit token path depth

Background token ID

WCAG contrast reference (e.g. color.background.default)

Tips

Run a compare before publishing library updates.

Use Figma File source to diff draft vs production libraries.

Use GitHub source to align Figma with your code repo before release.

Check Inspector → Impact before changing widely used tokens.

Pay attention to alias break warnings when editing base/global tokens.

Requirements & limitations

Works with Figma Variables (not legacy styles only).

GitHub and Figma File sources need network access and valid tokens.

Figma cross-file requires Enterprise and file_variables:read.

Token IDs must match between sources for accurate diffing.

Removed tokens are shown in the diff but not deleted from your file on apply.
model.tagline: Compare, review, and selectively apply design token changes — like a diff tool for Figma Variables.

Import JSON Tokens

model.name: Tokens Studio for Figma
model.description:
Gives you the ability to use Design Tokens that can be used for a whole range of design options, from border radii or spacer units to semantic color and typography styles that are able to reference other tokens. It allows you to change tokens and see these changes applied to the whole document, its styles or just a selection.


Generate Tokens with the UI or with your own JSON. Create or update Type, Color or Shadow Styles based on tokens. Reference tokens in each other to create type scales, container paddings or semantic colors.


Supported Tokens

  1. Colors (Fill, Border Color — hex, rgba, hsla) incl. color modifiers such as lighten, darken, mix or alpha
  2. Spacing (Horizontal, Vertical, Gap)
  3. Sizing (Width/Height)
  4. Dimension (spacing, sizing, radii, background blur)
  5. Opacity
  6. Typography (Font family, font weight, font size, line height, letter spacing, paragraph spacing)
  7. Shadow tokens (both dropShadow and innerShadow)
  8. Border tokens (color, width, strokeStyle)
  9. Border Radius (individually or each corner)
  10. Border Width
  11. Asset tokens (image fill)
  12. [Pro]: Composition tokens (think css classes for Figma)


All tokens support references to one another, so for example if you want to alias {theme.primary} to colors.blue then you'd write {colors.blue}

as a value.


Also, you can create math equations in tokens, allowing you to write a type scale like this: {fontSizeBase} * 1.618 and so on.


Find out more about Tokens Studio for Figma (Figma Tokens): tokens.studio and read the docs at docs.tokens.studio


Pro plan

To support teams that embrace this plugin we recently launched a Pro plan that comes with advanced features such as connecting tokens to Figma Styles, Multi-file sync, Advanced theme management, a branch switcher and composition tokens. If you rely on the plugin in your job, consider switching to the Pro plan to support the development of the plugin - we'll be able to ship new features faster for both the Pro and the Free version.


Usage guide

Create or update your Color or Text styles by creating tokens and then clicking Create Styles - use Styles as you were using them before.

Import existing styles to Tokens by clicking Import.

Left-click on a token to apply it to one or more layers.

Right-click a token to apply it to a specific property (such as only to Horizontal Spacing) - also you can delete or edit tokens by right-clicking them.


Example document

We've recently published an example document to play with if you're just getting started. We recommend to start the plugin in that file so you can see what you can do with the plugin.


Download free community file




Import your styles

Best way to get started is to just Import your existing styles as Tokens. Hit the "Import Styles" button on the top right.


Sync with external source of truth

  1. JSONBin
  2. URL (Read-only)
  3. GitHub
  4. GitLab
  5. Azure DevOps
  6. Supernova


This plugin is open source! Feel free to contribute, create suggestions at https://github.com/tokens-studio/figma-plugin

model.name: Interplay
model.description:
Interplay imports your design system code repository and lets you design with code components and design tokens in Figma.


With the Interplay plugin you can browse all of your design system code components, add them to your design in Figma, edit their content and all of the Code Component properties.


Interplay generates a Figma component on the fly and keeps it connected with the related code component so that your design is always in sync with your production code.


You can use all your design tokens directly in Figma — including tokens for border radius, padding, gap, etc. with our plugin. Or, you can generate Figma styles from your color, shadow, and typography tokens, and use those if you prefer.


What’s new?


Live rendering on the canvas. You can now edit components that have already been added to the canvas.


On canvas editing. You can now edit content directly on the canvas. When you edit a text box on the canvas, the Code Component property will be updated automatically.


On canvas resizing. To resize a component, you can now resize it directly on the canvas in Figma. When you resize a component, Interplay renders the code component in a browser in the background, and translates that layout back into Figma.


UI Improvements. We’ve made lots of UI updates to make it easier to browse components and edit properties


Quick Start


1. So that you can try out Interplay straight away, we’ve configured some open source libraries for you to get started including BaseUI. Select a design system and start dragging components onto the canvas.


2. To edit content and Code Component properties, select any component on the canvas and the plugin will display all of the the available code properties for the component.


Using your own design system in Figma with Interplay


We are gradually rolling out access to the Interplay CLI tool and Design System Manager which lets can import your own design system to Interplay. We are gradually rolling out access to teams.


Sign up for updates from within the plugin or by going to interplayapp.com

model.name: Token Master
model.description:
The plugin for Figma automates your color design tokens. With Token Master, you can edit styles in design tokens and quickly create new color modes. Just pick tokens with the same color and edit them at once!


How it works

  1. Install Token Master
  2. Download all styles from your file or add a new color mode. Use keywords [light] and [dark] in your style names to add a new color mode. Example: [light]Style name/ [dark]Style name
  3. To edit a style, click on it. Then, you can use the eyedropper or the color picker in the modal window to select a color
  4. Also, you can copy the whole group of your design tokens and create a new color mode


Styles name examples

We recommend using [light] / [dark] at the beginning of the style name:

[light] Color name 
[dark] Color name


But you can use [light] / [dark] at any place of your style name:

Color name [light]
Color name [dark]
Style / color-name [light]
Style / color-name [dark]
Style [light] / color-name
Style [dark] / color-name
